title: Staff Software Engineer (Agentic Search) - Index
descriptionHtml:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Product

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.

We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to work on the indexing and data processing layer of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on building systems that ingest, process, and organise massive volumes of data into efficient, queryable structures. You will work primarily on offline and nearline pipelines, ensuring that data is fresh, complete, and efficiently accessible by downstream retrieval systems. You will operate in an environment where throughput, scalability, and correctness are critical; designing systems capable of handling tens of gigabytes per second across continuously evolving datasets.

In this position, your responsibility will be to:

  • Design, implement, and operate large-scale indexing systems and data pipelines that sit at the core of our search infrastructure
  • Develop and optimise indexing strategies balancing performance, freshness, and resource efficiency
  • Work on storage formats, compaction strategies, and update mechanisms to keep data accessible and current
  • Ensure reliability and predictability of pipelines under high-throughput conditions
  • Build well-tested components with clear responsibilities and interaction contracts, while remaining flexible as the system evolves
  • Define and implement observability primitives, including structured logs, metrics, and data quality signals across offline and nearline pipelines
  • Monitor throughput, resource usage, and cost, and drive optimisations when business needs require it
  • Collaborate with runtime and ML teams to ensure indexing outputs meet retrieval and ranking requirements
  • Enable safe experimentation on indexing strategies and data processing logic through controlled rollouts and clearly defined quality signals

You may be a good fit if you:

  • 8+ years of experience building production backend or data infrastructure systems
  • Strong Go experience (C++/Rust is a plus)
  • Experience with large-scale data processing systems (10+ GiB/sec throughput, petabyte-scale datasets, etc.)
  • Experience building or operating databases, storage systems, data planes, or indexing pipelines
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, fault tolerance, consistency, and scalability
  • Experience running production systems and handling operational incidents
  • Systems-thinking mindset and ability to reason about end-to-end data flows

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

  • Distributed data processing frameworks such as Spark, Flink, MapReduce, or Beam
  • Content systems including, scraping, proxying, or anti-bot infrastructure
  • Ad tech, social networks, or other large-scale content platforms
  • DBMS internals (open source or SaaS) and cloud infrastructure
  • Open-source contributions or active involvement in the engineering community
  • Competitive programming or CTF participation (ICPC, IOI, or similar)
  • SHAD or similar advanced technical programmes
  • Conference talks or technical publications

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

title: Stage de Master 2 : Comprendre les transformations structurales des hydrates de sels inorganiques pour le stockage d’énergie thermochimique - 5 à 6 mois
descriptionHtml:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacuna l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur.

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

En tant que stagiaire de Master 2, vous êtes au cœur de nos missions de formation, recherche et innovation, au sein du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF, UMR CNRS 5307), Centre SPIN. Dans ce laboratoire, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal. Le LGF est une unité mixte de recherche CNRS et Mines Saint-Étienne. Il étudie la structure, les propriétés et la réactivité des matériaux, des poudres aux procédés énergétiques. Sa force : relier ce qui se passe à l’échelle du cristal à la performance d’un procédé.

Le stockage d’énergie thermochimique stocke la chaleur sous forme d’énergie chimique, grâce à des réactions solide-gaz réversibles. Les hydrates de sels inorganiques absorbent de la chaleur lors de leur déshydratation et la restituent lors de leur réhydratation, ce qui en fait des matériaux candidats pour le stockage de chaleur. Leur performance en cyclage dépend des structures cristallines traversées entre les états d’hydratation, dont le volume de maille et la symétrie peuvent différer fortement.

Les caractérisations ex situ, avant et après réaction, ne donnent accès qu’aux états extrêmes, pas au chemin de transformation. Ce stage suivra la transformation in situ afin d’identifier quelles phases apparaissent, dans quel ordre et avec quelle cinétique, et de comprendre pourquoi la réhydratation peut rester incomplète. Les hydrates de SrBr₂ servent de système modèle ; l’approche s’étend à d’autres hydrates de sels et à d’autres réactions gaz-solide.

• Vous réalisez une revue de la littérature sur les hydrates de sels pour le stockage thermochimique.

• Vous menez des cycles de déshydratation/réhydratation suivis par diffraction des rayons X in situ, sous température et humidité contrôlées.

• Vous quantifiez les fractions de phases par affinement de Rietveld (TOPAS, GSAS-II).

• Vous reliez structure et performance (fraction récupérée, vitesse de réaction, stabilité en cyclage).

• Vous rendez compte de vos résultats dans un mémoire et une présentation orale, avec une publication possible.

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et faire dialoguer expérimentation, structure et performance sera essentielle pour réussir.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Vous préparez un diplôme Bac + 5 (Master 2 ou dernière année d’école d’ingénieurs) en science des matériaux, physique, chimie du solide ou génie des procédés.

title: Stagiaire Chargé de mission – Accompagnement au changement & formation du SAS H/F
descriptionHtml:
L’Agence du Numérique en Santé (ANS) accompagne la transformation numérique du système de santé en France. Elle œuvre, aux côtés de ses partenaires institutionnels et professionnels, à garantir la confiance dans le numérique en santé, à sécuriser les échanges de données et à promouvoir des outils au service de la qualité des soins et du pilotage du système de santé.

Vous rejoindrez l’équipe déploiement, formation et support de la plateforme numérique du Service d’Accès aux Soins (SAS), au sein de la Direction Territoires et Expérience clients (DTEX). Le SAS facilite l’accès à un professionnel de santé lorsque le médecin traitant n’est pas disponible, pour des besoins de soins urgents ou non programmés. Développée par l’ANS, la plateforme numérique nationale aide les professionnels participant au SAS à identifier l’offre de soins disponible et à orienter les patients vers une prise en charge adaptée. Vous contribuerez à améliorer l’appropriation de la plateforme dans les territoires, à structurer les formations et à accompagner plusieurs chantiers opérationnels et de pilotage.

🎯 Missions principales

Développer l’espace de formation et accompagner les usages

  • Recenser et organiser les supports existants : formations, webinaires, documents, outils et présentations.

  • Construire la feuille de route et le calendrier de création du nouvel espace de formation, puis produire ou adapter des supports visuels, documents, guides et vidéos selon les profils utilisateurs.

  • Concevoir des outils d’évaluation des formations, analyser les retours et proposer des ajustements pour faciliter l’adoption de la plateforme.

Accompagner les professionnels et contribuer au pilotage

  • Participer aux réunions, webinaires, ateliers et formations avec l’équipe et les acteurs territoriaux.

  • Finaliser l’accompagnement des organisations et établissements dans l’enregistrement des opérateurs de soins non programmés (OSNP) au RPPS+, notamment en construisant un processus et un outil de suivi.

  • Assister le Product Owner dans la mise en œuvre du système d’information décisionnel (SID) de la plateforme : suivi et coordination des travaux de développement au regard des besoins métiers.


🧑‍🎓 Profil recherché

  • Vous êtes étudiant·e en études supérieures, de niveau Bac+4 ou Bac+5, dans un cursus en gestion de projet, communication, ingénierie pédagogique ou domaine équivalent.

  • Vous êtes à la recherche d’un stage de 6 mois à partir de janvier 2027.

  • Vous avez un intérêt pour la création de supports pédagogiques et visuels, la structuration de parcours de formation et la gestion de projet.

  • Vous êtes curieux·se, créatif·ve et capable d’analyser des situations complexes dans un environnement santé et numérique.

  • Vous appréciez le contact humain, savez écouter des interlocuteurs variés et comprendre leurs besoins pour proposer des réponses adaptées.

  • Vous êtes organisé·e et à l’aise pour coordonner plusieurs actions et en assurer le suivi.

title: Strategic Account Executive - London
descriptionHtml:

We’re looking for a Strategic Account Executive to join our founding GTM team and drive our next wave of growth, win new logos, and expand deals. You’ll own the full sales cycle, working with C-level executives at multibillion-dollar companies to transform how their businesses operate.

Success in this role goes well beyond closing deals. You’ll need to deeply understand each customer’s business, challenge their thinking, and work with them to build tailored solutions that fundamentally change how they work.

  • Move Fast – Act decisively, iterate quickly, optimize for momentum.

descriptionHtml:

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Strategy & Operations Lead of Doit Lithuania, you will build and run the business in Lithuania and grow it across the European Economic Area.

You will be the first senior hire in Lithuania. You will own the regulatory relationship, the build of the team, the partner network and the launch. You will sit on the management board and lead the business day to day.

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

title: Strategy & Operations
descriptionHtml:
Deducta

Strategy & Operations

Location: London, UK, near London Bridge. Hybrid, 3-4 in-person days a week.

Compensation: £90k-£110k base salary plus equity

Visa Sponsorship: Available for the right candidate

Start Date: As soon as possible

Why we exist

Every decision a business makes, from the suppliers it trusts to the risks it accepts, eventually shows up as spend. This makes spend data the most honest record of how a company operates. Not the strategy deck or the org chart: spend describes what really happened.

This record exists, but it's scattered across dozens of systems and decades of legacy technology. Companies spending billions a year still can't easily answer: Who are our suppliers? Where are we exposed? What are we paying for twice?

We believe a business that can't see itself clearly can't make great decisions. Deducta exists to give the world's most complex organisations a true picture of how they operate, and the intelligence to act on it. Our ambition is to become the category-defining platform for enterprise data intelligence.

We're well funded, growing fast, and have already processed more than £1 trillion of spend for some of the world's largest and most recognisable companies. Our partners use Deducta to deliver major business transformations orders of magnitude faster.

Why this role matters

Deducta is growing fast, and the work that keeps a company running well at this pace rarely belongs to one function. This role works directly with the Chief of Staff on the company's top priorities, turning them into plans, decisions and results. You'll report to the Chief of Staff.

You'll have broad scope and real autonomy, moving between operating cadences, cross-functional projects, investor materials and analysis for the leadership team. You'll see how every part of the company works and help shape how it runs.

What you'll do

  • Company priorities: Turn the leadership team's priorities into clear plans with owners, milestones and measures, and keep them on track.

  • Operating cadences: Run and improve how we plan, set goals and review progress, from weekly leadership meetings to quarterly planning.

  • Cross-functional projects: Lead projects that span GTM, customer delivery and hiring, from scoping the problem through to results.

  • Board and investor materials: Prepare board decks, investor updates and the analysis behind them.

  • Analysis for leadership: Build the models, benchmarks and recommendations the leadership team uses to make decisions.

Success in this role means:

  • Priorities deliver: Company priorities have clear owners and plans, and progress is visible without chasing.

  • Cadences work: Planning and review cycles run on time and lead to decisions rather than status updates.

  • Projects land: Cross-functional projects finish with measurable results, and the processes they create keep working.

  • Trusted analysis: Leadership relies on your analysis and recommendations for its most important decisions.

Who you are

We're looking for a high-agency former management consultant with roughly three to four years in MBB or top-tier management consulting, ideally having reached Manager. You'll combine structured problem solving with the drive to execute. A background in procurement or enterprise software isn't required.

You might be the right fit if you have:

  • Top-tier consulting experience: Roughly three to four years at MBB or a top-tier strategy firm, with experience leading workstreams and working with senior clients.

  • Structured problem solving: You take an ambiguous problem, break it down and turn it into a clear plan with owners and milestones.

  • Analytical depth: You build models and analysis yourself, and turn them into clear recommendations.

  • Strong execution: You follow through on details, keep many workstreams moving at once, and build processes that run without you.

  • Executive communication: You write and present clearly to senior audiences, including boards and investors.

  • Range: You're comfortable moving between strategy and hands-on operations in the same week.

  • Nice to have: Startup or in-house strategy experience, or exposure to B2B software, data or AI.

We care most about how you think, the quality of your work and how you approach unfamiliar problems. Previous startup experience isn't essential, but the pace, initiative and judgement to thrive in one are.

How we work

We believe in freedom and responsibility. We set clear priorities, share the context and trust people to decide how to deliver. You'll thrive here if you value:

  • Ownership: You own the outcome, not just the task. You deliver what you commit to, follow through when things get difficult, and own your mistakes.

  • Unreasonable hospitality: You treat prospects, clients and teammates with exceptional care as a default. You anticipate needs, communicate with clarity, and help others succeed.

  • Bias for action: We don’t have every answer upfront. You move things forward without waiting to be asked, take calculated risks, and adapt as you learn.

  • Craft: Moving quickly matters, but so does doing work that stays clear, reliable and useful as we grow.

  • System building: You create leverage beyond your own output, building processes, tools and documentation that others reuse and that keep working without you.

  • Candor: You tell the hard truth early, give and receive feedback thoughtfully, ask for help when you need it, and push back when priorities need to change.

  • Curiosity about AI: You’re excited by what applied AI makes possible, and you look for ways to use it in your own work.

As an early team member, you'll help shape our culture, our processes and where Deducta goes next. We're growing quickly, and this role will grow with us.

Hiring process

  1. Intro call

  2. Background interview

  3. Technical exercise

  4. Final interview

  5. Offer, referencing and start

Ob du schon Senior bist oder gerade richtig Fahrt aufnimmst, ist uns ehrlich gesagt zweitrangig. Bei uns zählt, was du baust und wie du an Probleme rangehst. Du bekommst echte Verantwortung, einen kurzen Draht zur Geschäftsführung und die Möglichkeit, dich so schnell weiterzuentwickeln, wie du selbst Gas gibst.

Aufgaben

  • Du planst, baust und betreibst Server- und Netzwerkumgebungen bei unseren Kunden und in unserer eigenen Cloud

  • Du betreibst unsere Cloud-Plattformen in deutschen Rechenzentren, von der Bereitstellung über Backup bis zum Monitoring

  • Du kümmerst dich um Firewalls, VPN und Netzwerk, damit alles sicher und sauber miteinander spricht

  • Du migrierst Kunden nach Microsoft 365 und richtest die Umgebungen so ein, dass sie auch in zwei Jahren noch sauber sind

  • Du betreust unsere Kundenumgebungen zentral, von Patching und Monitoring bis Endpoint-Security und Backup

  • Du baust Server und Workstations zusammen, prüfst sie auf Herz und Nieren und lieferst sie beim Kunden aus

  • Du bist Ansprechpartner für unsere Kunden, wenn etwas hakt, vom kurzen Anruf bis zur kniffligen Störung, und dokumentierst Lösungen so, dass auch der nächste durchblickt

  • Du redest bei Standards, Tooling und unseren Abläufen aktiv mit und automatisierst, was sich wiederholt

  • Du sprichst direkt mit Kunden, wenn es um Anforderungen, Konzepte und Lösungen geht

Wir wollen wachsen und unsere Infrastruktur-Standards mit uns. Wenn du Lust hast, am Fundament mitzubauen, bist du bei uns genau richtig.

Und keine Sorge, du sitzt mit deinen Problemen nicht allein da. Egal ob hartnäckige Störung, Architekturentscheidung, die du hinterfragen willst, oder einfach mal kurz Gedanken sortieren: Es ist immer jemand da, der mit dir draufschaut.

Qualifikation

  • Erfahrung mit Windows Server, Virtualisierung und Netzwerken

  • Du fühlst dich in Microsoft 365 wohl

  • Firewalls, VPN und Routing sind für dich keine Fremdworte

  • Du hast Bock auf Linux und Skripting

  • Du schraubst gern selbst an Hardware und baust Server lieber auf, als sie nur auszupacken

  • Du telefonierst gern mit Kunden und erklärst Technik so, dass sie am anderen Ende auch ankommt

  • Du lernst gern dazu, packst Dinge selbst an und bleibst auch dran, wenn es mal hakt

  • Herausforderungen schrecken dich nicht ab, sondern reizen dich eher

  • Du übernimmst gern Verantwortung und triffst Entscheidungen, statt auf Ansagen zu warten

  • Teamgeist ist für dich kein Buzzword, sondern Alltag

  • Du bist ehrlich und sagst, was du denkst

  • Führerschein Klasse B und Reisebereitschaft, weil unsere Kunden nicht nur um die Ecke sitzen und du regelmäßig vor Ort bist

Für uns zählen Persönlichkeit, Motivation und Potenzial mehr als ein dicker Stapel Zertifikate. Ob Junior oder Senior: Wichtig ist, dass du sauber baust und Lust hast, besser zu werden.

Benefits

Hardware, die Spaß macht. Leistungsstarke Workstations, ein eigenes Lab und lokale KI-Power statt Standard-Office-Laptop. Dazu ein voll ausgestatteter Firmenbulli für Einsätze vor Ort.

Eigener Firmenwagen. Nach der Probezeit bekommst du deinen eigenen Firmenwagen. So bist du für Kundentermine flexibel unterwegs und musst dir um dein eigenes Auto keine Gedanken machen.

Moderne Tooling-Kultur. Aktueller Stack, KI-gestütztes Arbeiten (unter anderem mit Claude) und kein Altlast-Ballast, der dich ausbremst.

Zertifizierungen auf uns. Wer sich bei unseren Herstellern zertifizieren will, bekommt Zeit und Budget dafür.

Wellpass oder Streaming-Abo. Sport in tausenden Studios deutschlandweit oder Spotify bzw. Netflix auf uns. Such dir aus, was zu dir passt.

30 Tage Urlaub. Volle 30 Tage, ohne Diskussion. Erholung gehört genauso dazu wie gute Arbeit.

Bildungsurlaub ist willkommen. Kein unangenehmes Gespräch, kein schlechtes Gewissen. Wer sich weiterbilden will, hat unsere volle Unterstützung.

Start-up-Flair. Kurze Entscheidungswege, echte Eigenverantwortung und eine Atmosphäre, in der Ideen mehr zählen als Hierarchien.

Flexible Arbeitszeiten. Leben und Arbeit muss man manchmal jonglieren. Dafür hast du bei uns Verständnis und Spielraum.

Home-Office. Nach der Einarbeitung arbeitest du da, wo du am produktivsten bist. Ob zu Hause oder im Büro, das entscheidest du.

Wenn du Teil eines Unternehmens sein möchtest, das nicht nur Wert auf technische Exzellenz legt, sondern auch auf deine persönliche Entwicklung, dann gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der IT!

title: Systems Engineer  (Excavator Automation)
descriptionHtml:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots.

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment.

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry.

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.


About the Job

The autonomy team at Gravis builds autonomous systems for excavators operating in real construction environments. This role is at the intersection of system engineering, integration, field deployments, and debugging.

We are looking for an engineer with a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Robotics or relevant fields and at least 2 years of practical, hands-on experience working with real systems - and if they fail, you can help us figure out why. This is not an entry-level or new-graduate role.

You will help define and execute system-level test scenarios, support atypical and beta deployments, and act as a technical bridge between the field and the engineering team. You will help train our field engineers and keep them in touch with fast evolving autonomy capabilities.
What you will do

  • Validate system behavior across machines, environments, and operating conditions

  • Identify edge cases, failure modes, and operational limits

  • Collaborate with engineering teams on making technical decisions on a system level

  • Investigate system failure during field testing or deployments

  • Apply hotfixes when appropriate

  • Support or conduct deployments if needed, especially pilots or beta customers

  • Support/conduct atypical deployments, pilots, and beta customers

  • Capture lessons learned from deployments and feed them back into system testing and design

  • Help prioritize fixes and improvements based on real-world impact


    • What we're looking for

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or a closely related field

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience working with complex systems (automation, robotics, vehicles, heavy machinery, industrial equipment, or similar)

  • Strong system-level troubleshooting and debugging skills

  • C++ and Python programming skills, proficiency in git systems

  • Proficiency in Linux systems

  • Comfortable working in field environments (construction sites, test yards, deployments)

  • Ability to travel abroad, according to needs of the business

  • Driver’s license B category


    • Beneficial

  • Experience with excavators, heavy equipment, or off-road vehicles

  • Field testing experience

  • Familiarity with communication technologies such as DDS, Zenoh, LCM etc.

  • Experience in motion planning or control

  • Experience in robotic competitions

    • Don't meet every requirement? If you're enthusiastic about this role but your experience doesn't match every qualification, we still encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect candidate for this or other positions.

    This is an opportunity to join a dynamic, multidisciplinary team and to be part of a company that is reshaping heavy construction.

    Gravis is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team, and do not discriminate based on race, colour, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics.

title: Talent Acquisition Intern
descriptionHtml:
Talent Acquisition Intern

Deine Mission bei trawa

Bei trawa sind wir überzeugt: Die Energiewende beginnt bei den Menschen, die sie möglich machen. Du willst leistungsstarke Teams mit aufbauen und Recruiting von Grund auf so lernen, dass es wirklich Wirkung hat? Dann bist du bei trawa genau richtig.

Als Talent Acquisition Intern bist du das operative Rückgrat unseres Talent-Teams und sorgst mit uns dafür, dass die richtigen Menschen zu trawa finden. Du hältst unsere Prozesse am Laufen, gestaltest reibungslose Candidate Journeys, räumst administrative Hürden aus dem Weg und hilfst, ein Hiring-Erlebnis zu bauen, das hängen bleibt. So bringst du direkt mit voran, was uns antreibt: Unternehmen den Zugang zu echter, grüner Energie zu ermöglichen.

Diese Rolle passt perfekt zu dir, wenn du Talent Acquisition hands-on lernen willst, gerne mit modernen Tools und KI-Lösungen arbeitest und direkt sehen möchtest, wie dein Beitrag das gesamte Team schneller und besser macht.

Bei uns findest du keine starren Strukturen - dafür Gestaltungsspielraum, Vertrauen und ein Team, das die Energiewende gemeinsam voranbringt.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

Was du bei uns vorantreibst

  • Bewerbungen screenen: Bewerbungen entlang klarer Basic Requirements checken und Kandidat:innen schnell und fair durch die Pipeline steuern.

  • ATS & Tracking: Unser ATS sauber, aktuell und strukturiert halten - plus einfache Tracker pflegen, damit alle jederzeit den Status im Blick haben

  • Interview-Organisation: Interviews end-to-end organisieren: Termine finden, Kalender koordinieren und das Team mit allen Infos versorgen.

  • Candidate Communication: Eine starke Candidate Experience sicherstellen - zeitnahe Updates geben, Fragen beantworten und durch den gesamten Prozess begleiten.

  • Interview-Flow: Feedback von Interviews schnell einsammeln, nachhalten und Stakeholder proaktiv erinnern.

  • Active Sourcing: Kandidat:innen vor allem über LinkedIn finden, erste Profileinschätzungen machen und die Ansprache übernehmen - damit aus „spannend“ schnell ein Gespräch wird.

  • Cross-functional Hiring supporten: Hiring über verschiedene Teams hinweg supporten (Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial) und dabei unterschiedliche Anforderungen & Profile verstehen lernen.

  • Team-Rituale & Ad-hoc: An Talent-Team-Routinen teilnehmen, Best Practices aufschnappen und spontan mit anpacken, wenn’s im Hiring gerade drauf ankommt

Wen wir suchen

  • Eingeschriebenes Studium, Gap Year oder Phase zwischen zwei Studienabschnitten

  • Lust darauf, Recruiting operativ stark aufzustellen und Hiring-Prozesse zu verbessern

  • Hands-on-Mentalität sowie Freude daran, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Themen verlässlich ins Ziel zu bringen

  • Empathisches, souveränes und professionelles Auftreten gegenüber Kandidat:innen und Stakeholdern

  • Strukturierte, detailgenaue Arbeitsweise mit gleichzeitigem Blick für das große Ganze

  • Fähigkeit, Prioritäten zu setzen und Timings zu koordinieren

  • Echtes Interesse an Menschen, Talent und Recruiting Operations

  • Erste Berührungspunkte mit Tools wie Google Calendar oder hohe Lernbereitschaft im Umgang mit neuen Tools

  • Affinität zu digitalen Tools und Automatisierung, um Recruiting smarter und effizienter zu gestalten

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und fließendes Englisch in Wort und Schrift

  • Standort in Berlin und Lust auf Zusammenarbeit in einem schönen Office im Herzen der Stadt

Warum trawa?

Du hilfst dabei, die Zukunft der Energiebranche mitzugestalten – und übernimmst Verantwortung für Themen, die echten Impact haben: auf unsere Hiring-Qualität, unsere Kultur und unser Wachstum. Als Talent Acquisition Intern legst du mit uns die Grundlage für ein Team, das auf Top-Niveau liefert – und trägst damit direkt zu unserer Mission bei.

Was dich erwartet

  • Impact ab Tag 1: Dein Beitrag beeinflusst Candidate Experience, unsere Talent Acquisition Prozesse und unsere Time-to-Hire spürbar

  • Gestaltungsspielraum: Recruiting-Operations mit aufbauen, Ideen umsetzen – keine starren Prozesse, sondern Verbesserungskultur

  • Onsite Zusammenarbeit: Unser Büro in Berlin-Mitte ist das Zentrum der Zusammenarbeit; Office-First-Kultur mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten

  • Klarer Rahmen: Mindestens 3 Monate (idealerweise 6 Monate) mit Option auf Übernahme in eine Vollzeitrolle (FTE)

  • Persönliche Entwicklung: End-to-end Recruiting lernen im Climate-Tech-Startup – Sourcing, Candidate Engagement, ATS-Hygiene, Prozess-Governance, Stakeholder Management

  • Diversity & Inclusion: Alle sind willkommen – wir leben ein inklusives Arbeitsumfeld, das Vielfalt wertschätzt

Über uns

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Unsere Mission ist es, den grünen Energieversorger der Zukunft von Grund auf zu bauen. Wie wir das schaffen? Wir ermöglichen B2B-Industrieunternehmen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie, entwickeln Software und Technologie zur Steuerung der Volatilität an Energiemärkten und professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

title: Talent Acquisition Manager
descriptionHtml:
Wir bauen humanoide Systeme: Full Stack, von Hardware und Elektronik über Software bis zur Fertigung, alles in-house in Berlin.

Bei Cell Labs verschieben wir die Grenze dessen, was Robotik leisten kann. Unser Ziel ist klar: Systeme bauen, die Menschen stärken statt sie zu ersetzen. Unsere Technologie ist bereits bei führenden Industriekunden und Partnern im Einsatz. Jetzt steht unser eigenes Produkt kurz vor dem Launch.

Die leise Phase ist vorbei. Wir suchen Menschen, die früh dabei sein wollen, Verantwortung übernehmen und das bauen, worüber andere nur reden.

Ort: Berlin · Start: Ab sofort · Arbeitsmodell: Vor Ort · Anstellung: Vollzeit

Deine Aufgaben

  • End-to-End Recruiting & Candidate Experience: Du verantwortest unsere Recruiting-Prozesse von der ersten Ansprache bis zur Einstellung. Du identifizierst passende Talente, prüfst eingehende Bewerbungen, führst strukturierte Interviews und koordinierst die nächsten Schritte. Dabei sorgst du für eine professionelle, transparente und wertschätzende Candidate Experience, auch bei hohem Bewerbungsaufkommen.

  • Hiring Manager Partnership: Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Gründern und Fachbereichen zusammen, definierst Anforderungen, erstellst passende Stellenanzeigen und stimmst Hiring-Zeitpläne ab. Du berätst zu Recruiting-Strategien, Marktbedingungen und Auswahlentscheidungen.

  • Offer Management, Onboarding & HR Support: Du begleitest Kandidaten durch die Angebotsphase, bereitest Vertragsunterlagen vor und koordinierst den Prozess bis zur Unterzeichnung. Du unterstützt das Onboarding und übernimmst bei Bedarf organisatorische HR-Aufgaben sowie die Betreuung von Kandidaten und Besuchern vor Ort.

  • Recruiting-Prozesse, Tools & KPIs: Du entwickelst effiziente, skalierbare Recruiting-Prozesse weiter und nutzt unser ATS, Automatisierung und KI-gestützte Tools. Du analysierst Kennzahlen wie Time-to-Hire, Pipeline Conversion und Offer Acceptance Rate, hältst Hiring Manager über Fortschritte auf dem Laufenden und leitest Verbesserungen ab.

  • Employer Branding & Recruiting Marketing: Gemeinsam mit unserem Marketing-Team stärkst du Cell Labs als Arbeitgebermarke, entwickelst überzeugende Recruiting-Inhalte und optimierst unsere Recruiting-Kanäle, um passende Talente auf uns aufmerksam zu machen.

  • Recruiting Events & Partnerschaften: Du entwickelst Events und Partnerschaften, die uns mit passenden Talenten verbinden, von Karrieremessen über Hochschulveranstaltungen bis zu kleinen Formaten bei uns im Office.

Was du mitbringst

  • Recruiting-Erfahrung: Du hast mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung im eigenständigen End-to-End Recruiting, idealerweise in einem schnelllebigen Startup, Scale-up oder internationalen, technologiegetriebenen Umfeld. Du kannst mehrere Recruiting-Prozesse parallel steuern und behältst auch bei hohem Bewerbungsaufkommen den Überblick.

  • Tech-Affinität: Du interessierst dich für komplexe Technologien und hast idealerweise bereits technische Positionen in Software, Engineering, Hardware oder anderen Tech-Bereichen besetzt. Du musst kein Engineer sein, solltest aber neugierig genug sein, technische Anforderungen wirklich zu verstehen.

  • Interviewkompetenz & Stakeholder Management: Du führst strukturierte, kompetenzbasierte Interviews, kannst Kandidaten fundiert einschätzen und gibst Hiring Managern klare Empfehlungen. Du kommunizierst souverän, hinterfragst Anforderungen konstruktiv und bringst unterschiedliche Perspektiven zusammen.

  • Prozesse, Daten & KI: Du arbeitest sicher mit modernen Recruiting-Tools und ATS-Systemen, kennst die relevanten Recruiting-KPIs und hast Freude daran, neue Technologien und KI-gestützte Lösungen auszuprobieren, um Recruiting effizienter und besser zu machen.

  • Arbeitsweise & Mindset: Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenständig und pragmatisch, übernimmst Verantwortung und findest auch bei wechselnden Prioritäten unkomplizierte Lösungen. Du bist empathisch, menschenorientiert und packst auch bei Aufgaben außerhalb deines eigentlichen Verantwortungsbereichs mit an.

  • Sprachen: Deutsch und Englisch verhandlungssicher.

Benefits

  • Recruiting mitgestalten: Du baust Recruiting in einem wachsenden Deep-Tech-Unternehmen aktiv mit auf. Du arbeitest direkt mit den Gründern und Fachbereichen zusammen, entwickelst Prozesse weiter und siehst, welchen Einfluss deine Arbeit auf unser Wachstum hat.

  • Alles unter einem Dach: Büro, Werkstatt und Teststände liegen im selben Gebäude in Kreuzberg. Wenn du ein technisches Profil besser verstehen oder erleben willst, woran unsere Engineers arbeiten, sind sie nur ein paar Schritte entfernt, kein Ticket.

  • Room to Fail & Grow: Bezahlte Lernzeit mit persönlichem Budget für Kurse, Recruiting-Konferenzen und die Tools, die du brauchst. Du bekommst Raum, Neues auszuprobieren, und hilfst dabei, ein Team aufzubauen, das Technologie entwickelt, die bisher kaum jemand gesehen hat.

  • Benefits: Ein Leistungspaket, das du dir selbst zusammenstellst und das Mobilität, Gesundheit, Ernährung oder Fitness abdeckt. Dazu gibt’s einen zusätzlichen bezahlten freien Tag im Jahr für ehrenamtliches Engagement oder ein Projekt, das dir am Herzen liegt.

Bewerbung

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und ein paar Zeilen zu einer Recruiting-Herausforderung, die du eigenständig gelöst hast. Welche Position oder Zielgruppe war besonders anspruchsvoll, wie bist du vorgegangen und was war das Ergebnis? Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht.

Der Prozess: Wird noch final abgestimmt.

Wir bauen Roboter für alle, deshalb wollen wir ein Team, das das abbildet. Wir stellen nach Fähigkeiten ein und freuen uns ausdrücklich über Bewerbungen von Menschen, die in Recruiting und Tech unterrepräsentiert sind. Wenn du nicht jeden Punkt erfüllst, aber denkst, das ist dein Job: bewirb dich.

title: Talent Partner
descriptionHtml:
Build the team that builds Conveo. As our London Talent Partner, you'll source and close top talent across the UK, US and Belgium as we scale past 100 people.

Conveo is a Y Combinator-backed company in an active growth period. We're scaling past 100 people and delivering our 2027 hiring plan. The people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how this company is built.

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We're investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

What We’re Building

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high-quality consumer and B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Canva use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing and product teams.

Traditional research is slow, expensive, and superficial. Running it well requires expertise most teams don't have. That gap affects how well companies understand their customers and how well they can serve them. We're closing it.

The Role

As Talent Partner at Conveo, you will build the team that builds the company. You'll join a small, lean talent team and play a big part in how we scale. You'll play a key part in how Conveo attracts, assesses, and ultimately hires talent across the US, UK, and Belgium, helping us scale past 100 people and deliver our 2027 hiring plan.

You'll close exceptional talent across engineering, product, go-to-market, and operations, while contributing to hiring strategy and talent decisions. You won't be limited to one area. You'll work with stakeholders and leadership across departments. If your experience leans towards one area, such as product and engineering, go-to-market, or operations, that's fine. We're open to candidates with a variety of backgrounds.

This isn't a transactional recruiting role. You'll shape how candidates experience Conveo and help build a team with high talent density for the long term. Proactive sourcing and strong execution will be central to your success.

Talent operations plays a small part in this role. Lots of foundations are already in place, and you'll help build on them as we scale. If you like to experiment and work with the latest tech, especially AI, you'll find this role really interesting.

We're growing fast, so priorities shift and you'll often make calls with imperfect information.

What You’ll Do

Own hiring outcomes end-to-end

  • Partner closely with hiring managers and leadership

  • Own roles from kickoff to close, including sourcing and closing

  • Maintain speed without sacrificing quality

  • Develop strong hiring judgment

Build proactive talent pipelines

  • Develop centralised talent pipelines across key disciplines, enabling the business to take a broader and more proactive approach to hiring

  • Create innovative sourcing strategies for particular searches, incorporating AI-enabled sourcing, targeted outbound campaigns, market mapping, events, and external communities

  • Proactively source top-tier talent using LinkedIn, Juicebox, and other tools. Our toolkit isn't fixed. We're always looking at new tools, and deciding whether to build them internally or use them externally, to level up our sourcing and recruitment capabilities.

  • Provide external talent intelligence, including candidate availability, competitor activity, compensation, and wider market trends

Build a high-signal candidate experience

  • Be the main point of contact and advocate for candidates

  • Every candidate hears back from us quickly, whether it's a yes or a no.

  • Pitch Conveo with real conviction, because you understand the product, the market and why people join.

Grow our employer brand

  • Contribute to employer branding content that shows what it's like to work at Conveo

  • Support events that put Conveo in front of top talent

Build scalable hiring and people systems

  • Improve interview loops, scorecards, and decision-making

  • Track funnel health

  • Maintain clean hiring and people data in Ashby (our ATS) and internal tools

  • Build repeatable playbooks and templates

What Success Looks Like

  • Hiring managers see you as a true partner and want you on their searches: you've added key players to their teams quickly and efficiently.

  • Hires that work out: you bring in the right people, and we can see who was hired and why they did well in the organisation.

  • Ownership of our hiring goals: you understand the hiring plan and your contribution to it. When blockers come up, you flag them and proactively work to fix them so we hit our goals.

  • Gaps found and closed: you work autonomously, but take time early on to understand what gaps exist and why, then work with the team to close them.

  • Better decisions over time: you make decisions in the moment with the best information available, even when the data isn't perfect, and push to gather more data so future decisions are better informed.

  • A better way of doing things: you challenge the status quo when something could be done in a way that's better for the business, drawing on your experience and backing it up with data and resources.

Your First 3 Months

  • You've taken ownership of a set of live roles and closed your first few hires.

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. title: TCS and ECLSS Certification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Mission

We are developing, manufacturing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable spacecraft which will carry cargo to space stations and potentially humans in the longer run.

We are seeking an experienced Certification Engineer to join our Thermal Control System & Environmental Control and Life Support System team. You will be responsible for leading, coordinating, and driving the certification and verification closure activities of the Nyx Thermal Control System (TCS) and Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) in support of vehicle qualification, NASA certification, and flight acceptance.

The role serves as the primary focal point between the TCS & ECLSS teams, System Engineering, Verification & Validation, Chief Engineering Office, AIT, Program, Safety Engineering, and external stakeholders. The Certification Engineer ensures that TCS and ECLSS requirements are properly allocated, verified, traceable, and closed with appropriate evidence, while maintaining alignment with NASA SSP requirements, Data Item Deliverables (DIDs), verification plans, and Safety Review Panel expectations.

The position requires a strong understanding of spacecraft systems engineering, thermal engineering, verification methodologies, qualification logic, and agency review processes to ensure that technical evidence across both subsystems is complete, credible, traceable, and accepted by the certification authorities.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Thermal & ECLSS Verification Closure Activities

  • Own the verification closure process for TCS and ECLSS, from subsystem level through spacecraft-level qualification.

  • Ensure TCS and ECLSS requirements are allocated to appropriate verification methods.

  • Coordinate the preparation, execution, and closure of verification events with analysts, product owners, subsystem engineers, system engineers, and test teams.

  • Maintain consistency between the TCS & ECLSS verification strategies and spacecraft-level verification planning.

  • Ensure analyses, test reports, inspection records, NCRs, requirement justifications, and review documentation are available to support certification closure.

  • Support the preparation of qualification, certification, and flight readiness reviews.

  • Ensure consistency of verification logic and evidence across TCS and ECLSS, particularly for requirements, interfaces, functions, or verification activities involving both subsystems.

Manage NASA Requirement Compliance and Verification Product

  • Act as the TCS & ECLSS focal point for NASA certification and verification activities.

  • Coordinate the closure of applicable NASA SSP requirements and associated verification products, including the DIDs.

  • Ensure consistency between analyses, test results, requirements, qualification rationale, and certification documentation across both subsystems.

  • Maintain alignment between NASA verification expectations and TEC verification approaches.

  • Coordinate with TCS and ECLSS technical owners to ensure certification evidence is technically robust and delivered according to program and customer milestones.

Lead Thermal & ECLSS Contributions to Safety Reviews

  • Prepare and coordinate TCS & ECLSS contributions to NASA Safety Reviews.

  • Ensure TCS and ECLSS hazards, controls, verification evidence, and closure rationale are fully documented.

  • Support and coordinate the development of safety review presentations and supporting technical packages.

  • Ensure consistency between hazard reports, verification evidence, and qualification activities.

  • Coordinate with Safety Engineering and subsystem technical owners to ensure certification evidence supporting hazard-control verification is identified and available.

Support Qualification and Test Campaigns

  • Ensure qualification, acceptance, development, and integrated test campaigns provide the evidence required for certification.

  • Identify verification gaps early and drive mitigation actions.

  • Support preparation of verification plans, qualification matrices, and closure notices.

  • Participate in major test reviews and assess certification impacts of anomalies and non-conformances.

  • Support requirement closure from TVAC, Thermal Balance, functional testing, and integrated spacecraft verification campaigns.

  • Drive the closure of actions and verification-related NCRs

 

Required Qualifications

Technical

  • MSc or equivalent degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.

  • Strong understanding of spacecraft thermal control system, ECLSS, and spacecraft development processes.

  • Experience with spacecraft verification and qualification methodologies.

  • Familiarity with NASA and/or ECSS verification standards, requirements management, verification matrices, and closure processes.

  • Understanding of thermal analyses, thermal testing, qualification logic, and evidence generation.

Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in spacecraft development, system engineering, verification, certification, or thermal engineering.

  • Experience supporting spacecraft design reviews and qualification campaigns.

  • Experience interfacing with external customers, agencies, or certification authorities.

  • Experience managing complex technical documentation and evidence packages.

Personal Skills

  • Strong organization, coordination, technical writing, and communication skills.

  • Ability to drive closure of multidisciplinary actions across engineering teams.

  • High level of rigor, traceability, and attention to detail.

  • Ability to challenge assumptions and ensure certification readiness.

  • Comfort presenting technical material to senior engineering leadership and external review boards.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?

title: Tech Ops Lead
descriptionHtml:
Hozah makes parking automatic. Our cameras recognise your car when you arrive and payment happens by itself when you leave. No apps, no tickets. We were named PayTech Company of the Year, we sit in Deloitte’s list of the 50 fastest growing tech companies in the UK, and we are expanding our estate of automated car parks across the country.

Every site runs on ANPR cameras, payment kiosks, edge devices and 4G connectivity, and all of it has to work around the clock. The TechOps team keeps that estate healthy. We are hiring the person to lead it.

The Role

This is a player-manager role, split roughly 50:50.

Half your week is leading our TechOps engineers: running 1:1s, setting standards, managing KPIs, coaching, and owning the service desk. You decide how technical problems get diagnosed and resolved at Hozah, and you hold the team to that standard.

The other half is hands-on engineering. When a client reports that revenue at a site has dropped 40% while every device shows healthy, you dig into the data, query the database, test the APIs and work out whether it is a bug, a misconfiguration or a camera problem. The systems are built in house, so there is no vendor to escalate to. TechOps own it through to resolution whether the problem lies in hardware, software or config and the fix is yours or a developer's. The software side is similar to L3 application support.

What you’ll be doing

  • Leading the service desk and developing a small team of TechOps engineers.

  • Personally investigating the hardest faults across cameras, networks, kiosks and our backend platform.

  • Using SQL, API testing and log analysis to get to the root cause of operational problems.

  • Improving monitoring and alerting so we catch degradation before it becomes an incident.

  • Technically assisting on new site launches: network design, hardware spec and commissioning.

  • Working closely with our Estate Manager, our developers and the COO to improve the estate week on week.

What we’re looking for

  • You manage a technical team today, or have very recently: real direct reports and real performance conversations, while staying hands-on yourself.

  • You have run a busy operation with high ticket volumes, multiple sites and live incidents, and kept on top of it.

  • You are an adept service desk manager: you know what to prioritise, when and what to escalate, and how to direct the team’s workflow so the queue keeps moving.

  • Your instinct is to investigate first: querying data, testing APIs, reading logs. L3 application support backgrounds fit this role well.

  • You have solid networking fundamentals (IP addressing, DNS, VPNs). Deep enterprise networking not needed.

  • You stay calm during live incidents and organised when several things need attention at once.

What this role isn’t

  • Corporate IT support. The users of our systems are cameras and cars, and the work is operating a distributed technology estate.

  • A pure management job. Half the week is engineering work, and we want someone who likes it that way.

  • Heavily process-bound. We are a scale-up, so you will build the processes we need as we grow.

Salary, location and working pattern

  • £50-60k depending on experience.

  • 3 days a week in our Croydon office, 2 days from home, with occasional site visits around the UK.

  • You report directly to the COO and own the new TechOps function.

title: Technical Director
descriptionHtml:
This is a permanent full-time remote opportunity for those based in the UK.

About Nearform
Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.  

As part of our Delivery Management function, you will help our clients build solutions and platforms, launch new product ventures, and fundamentally change how they operate.

You will work as part of a highly skilled, multidisciplinary team, typically consisting of designers, developers, DevOps engineers, and members of the client team.

Whether you’re a Delivery Manager, Technical Lead, or Technical Director, you will act as the bridge between client needs and timelines, ensuring the delivery of innovative, scalable solutions.

About the Technical Director role

As a Technical Director at Nearform, you will provide strategic and technical leadership across multiple projects, ensuring alignment with business goals while fostering innovation and excellence. Your role will involve technical vision-setting, client engagement, and team leadership to drive both project success and long-term growth.

  • Technical Strategy & Leadership – Define and communicate a clear technical vision, ensuring best practices in architecture, software development, and emerging technologies. Act as the final authority in critical design and delivery decisions.
  • Client Engagement & Advisory – Serve as a trusted advisor to CIOs, CTOs, and senior stakeholders. Lead discovery workshops, translate business objectives into technical strategies, and develop tailored solution proposals.
  • Project Execution & Delivery – Oversee technical execution, ensuring quality, scalability, and maintainability. Monitor project health, identify risks, and ensure successful outcomes through proactive leadership.
  • Team Leadership & Talent Development – Work with resourcing teams to ensure the right talent is staffed on projects. Foster a culture of excellence, mentorship, and innovation across teams.
  • Financial & Operational Oversight – Manage project burn-down, optimize resource allocation, and identify revenue growth opportunities while maintaining financial accountability.
  • Industry Influence & Thought Leadership – Stay ahead of industry trends, contribute to open-source projects, and engage in public speaking, blog writing, and mentorship. Champion Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) and sustainability initiatives within Nearform.

What we are looking for in this person

  • 15+ years of technical leadership experience, ideally within consulting, SaaS, or large-scale digital transformation projects.
  • Deep expertise in software architecture, cloud platforms, and modern development practices.
  • A strong track record of guiding technical decisions on complex, high-impact projects.
  • Experience leading pre-sales, discovery, and solution design discussions.
  • Strong ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • A consultative mindset, able to align business needs with technical strategies.
  • Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills to influence at all levels.
  • Hands-on experience with AI, databases, distributed systems, and modern software engineering best practices.
  • Experience leading and mentoring senior software development teams
  • A passion for continuous learning, innovation, and professional excellence.

Preferred Skills

  • Previous experience working in a fully remote, globally distributed environment.
  • Background in financial oversight of technology projects.
  • Experience contributing to open-source projects or technical thought leadership.
  • Prior exposure to AI-driven solutions and emerging technologies.

Benefits & Perks

  • Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance.
  • Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!
  • Paid Time Off Package - We offer an annual leave of 25 days plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
  • Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in GBP) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
  • Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval.
  • Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
  • Pension & Insurances - We offer a pension match of up to 5% and Income Protection and Death in Service for peace of mind.

Our Interview Process

  • Talent Call (30 mins, Zoom)An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.
  • Hiring Manager Interview (1 hour, Zoom)A conversation with the Head of Delivery or CTO focused on your approach to delivery management, client collaboration, and technical problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.
  • Panel Interview (1.5 hours, Zoom)
    A discussion with 2 Technical Directors focusing on your team leadership and delivery management approach in more detail. This includes scenario-based questions on team management, delivering technical work, and client collaboration, assessing how you drive success in an enterprise development environment.
  • Final Interview (45 mins, Zoom)A final chat with the Managing Director for the region to discuss the plans for this role, Nearform’s strategy, and any questions you may have.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

As part of our recruitment process, we conduct manual and electronic identity verification checks to confirm the identity of prospective employees.


Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence. 

If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

title: Technical Lead
descriptionHtml:
Technical Lead

Location: Bristol (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Team: Engineering

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Software Engineering Manager

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

The role

You’ll join the Kaluza Technology community: a large team of product-focused and data-led Product and Platform Engineers working at serious scale. Our ecosystem is primarily based on TypeScript and React, utilising GraphQL and Kafka, backed by AWS and Terraform. Our work and responsibilities are diverse and wide-ranging, so you will need to have a product-minded problem solving attitude first and foremost. As a Senior Engineer you’ll own a slice of the product end-to-end, from the first design conversation to running it in production, and you’ll build it with AI coding agents as your default. We’re looking for someone whose judgement is worth more than their typing speed.

Engineers at Kaluza build with AI, and we mean that practically. From your first day you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and MCP access to the systems you need. Our tooling and conventions are evolving quickly, and you’ll have a heavy hand in defining how we build moving forward.

What you’ll do

  • Set the technical direction for your team: be accountable for the solution designs and architecture decisions, work with your team on technical strategy, and assist them through ambiguity over the longer term.

  • Work across the stack over time: depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.

  • Build with AI coding agents as your default: break work down so agents can execute it, direct them, review what they produce as carefully as a colleague’s PR, and maintain the tests and guardrails that let agent-written code merge safely.

  • Own the health of your services: SLOs and SLAs, operational health reviews, post-mortems, and the in-hours support rota, with your turn on the on-call rota alongside the team.

  • Coach the engineers around you: technical guidance for a mix of junior and senior engineers, pairing, and code review that teaches as well as gates.

  • Connect your team to the rest of Kaluza: work with other Tech Leads and Principal Engineers on the wider architecture, and represent your team where platform decisions and engineering standards are made.

What you’ll bring

These are the practices and behaviours we see most in our best tech leads and value deeply, but we don’t expect everyone to tick every single box. If you’re excited by the role and can see yourself thriving here, we’d love to hear from you.

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Experience with our tech stack: TypeScript and React, utilising GraphQL and Kafka, backed by AWS and Terraform.

  • Experience leading technical change: you’ve taken a new service or a major architecture change from idea through to running in production, and you can say what you’d do differently.

  • A daily agentic development practice: you build with tools like Claude Code or Cursor, you can walk us through work you’ve shipped this way, and you have views on where agents help a team and where they get in the way.

  • Operational ownership: comfortable deploying with shared tooling, well-versed in SRE fundamentals like SLOs, disaster recovery and platform health monitoring, and used to owning your software in production, including out-of-hours on-call.

  • A coach’s instincts: you’ve mentored and grown engineers at different levels, and you make the people around you better.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to action: you can deliver against a technical strategy iteratively over months, and you’d rather ship a sound first step than wait for certainty.

  • Strong product sense: you ask why before building, and you can point to times when user feedback or metrics changed what you shipped.

  • Clear communication, especially in writing: designs, specs, PR descriptions and post-mortems that a teammate, a stakeholder or an agent can act on, and the stakeholder skills to work well with Product Managers, Principal Engineers and other Tech Leads.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

Vous intervenez notamment sur les missions suivantes :

  • Concevoir et faire évoluer les produits en tenant compte des contraintes techniques, industrielles et réglementaires ;
  • Réaliser les plans et les études techniques et vérifier la faisabilité des solutions proposées ;
  • Concevoir de petits outillages et supports de production et suivre leur fabrication ;
  • Participer au pilotage des projets : planning, budget, fournisseurs et sous-traitants ;
  • Réaliser ou suivre les essais mécaniques nécessaires à la validation des produits ;
  • Participer à la constitution et au suivi des dossiers de certification et d'extension de produits ;
  • Vérifier la conformité des produits aux normes applicables et assurer une veille sur leurs évolutions ;
  • Réaliser les études de prix de revient pour les demandes spécifiques ;
  • Travailler en lien étroit avec la production, la qualité, les fournisseurs et les autres services de l'entreprise.

Vos compétences

Vous êtes issu(e) d'une formation technique de niveau Bac+2 minimum en conception mécanique, bureau d'études, industrialisation, génie mécanique ou domaine similaire.

Vous disposez idéalement de plusieurs années d'expérience dans un environnement industriel et avez une première expérience en conception ou en bureau d'études.

Nous sommes également ouverts à des profils issus des méthodes ou de l'industrialisation, disposant d'une bonne maîtrise technique et souhaitant évoluer vers un poste davantage orienté conception et développement produit.

Vous êtes à l'aise avec la lecture de plans et les outils de conception/dessin industriel.

La connaissance des normes, des essais mécaniques ou des processus de certification constitue un plus. Une formation pourra être assurée sur les spécificités de notre activité.

  • Rigueur et sens de l'organisation ;
  • Esprit d'analyse et capacité à rechercher des solutions techniques ;
  • Autonomie dans la conduite des projets ;
  • Goût pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes ;
  • Capacité à travailler avec différents interlocuteurs ;

Participation/Intéressement – Chèques déjeuner – Avantages CE

Pourquoi rejoindre NADIA SIGNALISATION ?

Vous intervenez sur des produits concrets, de leur conception à leur fabrication, avec un rôle transversal entre Bureau d'Études, production, fournisseurs et qualité.

Vous aurez également l'occasion de développer une expertise dans un domaine technique spécifique, notamment sur les normes, essais et certifications de produits de signalisation.

title: Trust Communications
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR

Millions of people build on Lovable, from software that runs new businesses to the tools that power existing ones. At the center of it all is trust. That’s why we’re looking for an exceptional storyteller to spearhead Lovable’s trust, safety, and security communications efforts.

Why Lovable

For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now.

Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too.

The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway.

What you’ll do

Build and own Lovable’s trust narrative. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned, new, and owned media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, and safety. You’ll shape the stories that highlight our commitments and ensure we show up in the conversations where trust in AI platforms is being decided right now.

Be the comms partner to our security and trust leadership. You’ll develop and own the spokesperson platforms for our CISO and other senior leaders who speak on our trust efforts, identifying and preparing them for on-stage and media opportunities. You’ll help them become recognized voices on topics of trust in AI software creation.

Own incident communications, end to end. When something doesn’t go as planned, you’re the incident comms lead who ensures clear and swift communications for every audience that needs to hear from us, including media, customers, and employees. You’ll build and run the playbook that lets us move faster each time.

Build relationships with relevant media and creators. You’ll know the voices who matter most in telling our trust story, and you’ll make sure those relationships exist before we need them.

Who you are

You’ve done trust, safety, or security communications. You have proven comms experience across a variety of trust-related topics, from AI safety to security. You’ve worked on or alongside security, privacy, or trust and safety teams.

You have real incident experience. You’ve been the incident comms lead more than once, and you’ve probably written a playbook along the way. You bring the attention to detail, precision, speed, and judgment an incident requires.

You have strong media relationships in the tech and AI ecosystem. Security and trust reporters, analysts, policy-adjacent media, perhaps even researchers. You know who they are, what they care about, and how to earn their attention honestly.

You’re voraciously curious. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need to be willing to understand how a platform like ours works well enough to describe an incident accurately and explain a safety decision without hand-waving.

You write clearly and have keen attention to detail. Your writing is precise, human, and accessible, even when the subject matter is complex or the situation is sensitive. You also catch things others may miss.

You’re calm, hands-on, and low-ego. You’ll draft the statements, build the media list, prep the spokesperson, and coordinate across teams yourself. You thrive in environments where the plan often changes and the pace is relentless.

You have 6+ years of experience in communications, with significant time spent on trust and safety, security, or incident communications at a technology company. We care more about the right years than the number of them: judgment under pressure matters more than tenure.

What you need to know

This is a strategic but hands-on role with both proactive and reactive components. That means you’ll need to be comfortable being the person who’s on call when something breaks, while simultaneously leading the charge on work that moves our trust narrative forward. The role itself lives at the intersection of several functions, and you’ll be the one finding the red thread among all that’s happening so we can tell a cohesive story externally.

Lovable is a European company with a global audience. The trust story has to resonate outside of Silicon Valley and our home turf in Stockholm. Wherever you sit, you’ll work across time zones and build relationships with the teams whose work you’re talking about.

Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you’re deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn’t technically “yours” when the moment calls for it.

Background:
In 2011, three students from TU Munich founded Celonis (www.celonis.com), today the global leader in Process Intelligence. Our mission: make Enterprise AI work. title: Verification Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At Ubitium, we believe the best engineering happens when people with different perspectives tackle hard problems together. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences. What matters most is curiosity, skill, and the drive to build technology that improves the world. If that resonates with you, we’d love to hear from you. Our team members come from some of the best universities in the world and left some of the largest tech companies to build something truly remarkable.

Tasks

  • Build cocotb-based testbenches for RTL blocks ranging from complicated datapaths to multilevel interconnect, driven by property-based test generation rather than fixed directed vectors.Write SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) to catch protocol violations directly in simulation, plus cover property statements to close functional-coverage gaps.
  • Cross-check RTL behavior against independent golden reference models (including formally-specified models) to catch divergence between spec intent and implementation
  • Drive functional coverage closure, reviewing coverage reports
  • Debug failures using waveform viewers and simulator transcripts, working from a failing assertion or model mismatch back to a root cause in the RTL, the testbench, or the model.
  • Document and track open verification findings (RTL bugs, model gaps, or verification-methodology limitations) with clear reproduction steps, so issues are shareable and actionable across the team.
  • Continuously improve the verification infrastructure itself (build flows, test harnesses, coverage tooling).

Requirements

  • Languages: System Verilog, System Verilog Assertions, Python.
  • Skills: RTL debugging, Property Based Verification, Git.
  • Good to have: Formal Verification exposure.

Master’s degree (or equivalent) and 2+ years of hands-on experience in a relevant role. Relocation required. Currently 4 days on-site, 1 day remote. Policy may change.

Benefits

  • A verification methodology you help shape, not just execute. The team builds its own property-based test harnesses, cross-checks RTL against formally-specified golden models, and wires up both SVA and native SystemVerilog covergroups. If you have opinions on how verification should be done, there’s real room to introduce them.
  • Direct, tight feedback loops with the architects/designers. Findings get written up, discussed, and resolved collaboratively. You’ll see your root-cause analysis directly inform (or get corrected by) the people who wrote the RTL.
  • Exposure across the full stack of a RISC-V SoC.
